classes.implemented: `src/` evaluates this condition NOW -- the field is kept current, not frozen at Task 39. `src.module`, `src.function` and `src.expr` name the construct that does, so the pairing is falsifiable by reading it, and `tools/test_combat_opener.py`'s `test_every_implemented_row_names_the_function_that_evaluates_it` requires every name in `src.expr` to occur inside that function's body. `src.expr` is a PARAPHRASE of the shipped expression, close enough to find it and never a substitute for opening the file -- `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` forbids citing a `src/` line number. classes.unimplemented: `src/` does not evaluate it, in the tree that ships this file. `what` says what it does, from flow. After Task 40 exactly two rows carry this class, and both are the never-taken compiler artefacts in `excluded_from_citation` -- there is no unported BEHAVIOUR left in `FUN_1000_3d11`'s uncited population.
classes.unreachable-in-port: the port deliberately diverges and `docs/re/gaps.md` records the divergence. NO ROW USES THIS CLASS -- see `unreachable_in_port_is_empty` below.

port_status.cited: Task 40 put this branch's address, or its guard's, on the `src/` construct that evaluates it -- either because Task 40 implemented the behaviour (the ten opener gates and the four agility-report gates) or because `src/` already implemented it and only the citation was missing. `tools/test_combat_opener.py` re-derives this from the citation index, so the label cannot be asserted onto a row.
port_status.never-cited: This branch is NOT cited and is not going to be: see `excluded_from_citation`. It is also exactly what a fresh recomputation still reports as uncited for this function.

unreachable_in_port_is_empty: Not one of these branches is unreachable in the port. The nearest candidates were checked and rejected: `1000:56ba` and `1000:5760` are branches that can never be TAKEN in the ORIGINAL (`mov al,1` / `or al,al` / `jz`), which is a compiler artefact and not a port divergence, so they stay `unimplemented`; and the four blow-budget report gates (`1000:3ff5`, `1000:4011`, `1000:4098`, `1000:40b4`) guarded two lines the port did not print, which was a missing feature and not a recorded divergence either -- **Task 40 implemented them, so those four are now `implemented` and this sentence records why they were never a divergence, not a present state.** An empty class is reported rather than filled, because using it as an escape hatch is how an inventory stops being falsifiable.

excluded_from_citation.ruling: Permanently excluded from `port_touched` by the Task 40 controller: a port cannot honestly evaluate a condition that is constant-true in the original, and writing the address beside code that decides something else would be a false citation -- worse than leaving the branch uncited, because it makes the map lie while the metric improves. So `FUN_1000_3d11`'s realistic ceiling is 222 of its 224 game branches, not 224.
excluded_from_citation.why_they_can_never_be_taken: Each is `mov al,1` / `or al,al` / `jz`: `al` holds the immediate 1 stored two instructions earlier, `or` clears ZF for any non-zero operand, so ZF is never set and the `jz` is never taken. Re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `test_the_two_never_taken_rows_are_excluded_from_citation`, which decodes the three instructions rather than trusting this sentence.

port_equivalences.original: the LAST link of a `cmp ax,N` chain over a `Random(n)` result -- `cmp ax,0x2` / `jnz` for the crit taunts and the charm table, `cmp ax,0x1` / `jnz` for the two-way ones
port_equivalences.here: the `_` arm of a Rust `match` on the same draw
port_equivalences.why_it_is_the_same_decision: the original DROPS a value the chain does not name and the `_` arm does not, so the two differ only on a result the draw cannot produce: `Random(3)` returns 0..2 and `Random(2)` returns 0..1, and `src/rng.rs` reproduces the same bound. A change to that bound, or a draw whose `n` grew, would break this equivalence -- which is why it is written down rather than assumed.

port_equivalences.original: `1000:4b6c cmp ax,0xa` / `1000:4b6f jnl 0x4bb3` on a SIGNED `hpmax - hp`
port_equivalences.why_it_is_the_same_decision: when hp > hpmax the original's `ax` is negative, `jnl` fails and it takes the branch that LOWERS hp to hpmax; `saturating_sub` gives 0, also < 10, so the port takes the same branch and makes the same assignment. `Game::smoke`'s doc comment carries the same table for the street copy of this handler.

port_equivalences.original: `rtl_str_compare` against the CS tokens `run` and `e`, after the case fold at `1000:4431`
port_equivalences.why_it_is_the_same_decision: `parse` folds `w` with `run` and `exit` with `e` because `entry` dispatches both spellings; the fight prompt compares only the short one, so matching the literal is what reproduces the original and using `parse` would not. `Game::run_combat`'s doc comment argues this at both sites.

port_equivalences_note: Where an `implemented` row's `src.expr` decides the same thing as the original by a DIFFERENT predicate. Each entry says why the two agree, and on what assumption -- an equivalence with no stated assumption is the kind of pairing a reviewer cannot falsify. `data/gym_arms.json`'s `joint.port_equivalences` is the shape this follows.

src_pairing_check.what: How strongly `tools/test_combat_opener.py` pins an `implemented` row's `src` block. The check requires every name in `src.expr` to occur inside the NAMED FUNCTION'S BODY, not merely somewhere in the module -- the module-wide version passed all 101 rows whatever function they named, which made it a guard against one symptom (a wrong MODULE) presented as the falsifier for the class (a wrong CONSTRUCT).
src_pairing_check.note: `rows_uniquely_pinned_floor` is a RATCHET, not an equality: the test asserts >=, so writing a more distinctive expression can only raise it and a weakened check reds. The measurement today is 69 of 115 rows pinned (46 not), and the floor is deliberately left at the 55-of-101 figure Task 39 recorded rather than raised to 69 -- see `vacuous_pins`, which is why 69 is not 69 discriminations. The 46 unpinned rows share their identifiers with a sibling function (e.g. Game::spoil_charm and Game::spoil_glasses both call below_at and both set has_mobile), so the check narrows them without isolating them. This is a filter, not a proof: whether the Rust expression computes the same ANSWER as the original's compare rests on each row's `what` and on a reviewer reading the pair.
src_pairing_check.fragility: The identifier test is a SUBSTRING search over the named function's whole body, comments included, so ordinary English words in a sibling function's prose can un-pin a row: Task 40's own citation comments put `rank`, `name`, `class` and the word `which` into `Game::run_combat` and `Game::spoil_blade` and dropped the count from 55 to 52 without touching a single `src.expr`.  The repair the ratchet's docstring names is the right one -- write a MORE DISTINCTIVE expression -- and it is what three rows got (`1000:41d1`, `1000:43bc`, `1000:5421`); lowering the floor is not.  Recording this because the next task to add prose here will hit it.
src_pairing_check.vacuous_pins: Ten of the pinned rows are Task 40's opener gates, whose module `src/combat_opener.rs` defines exactly ONE function they name. The test's rule is 'no OTHER function this module's rows name accepts this expression', and with no other function that is vacuously true -- so those ten pin for want of a sibling rather than by discrimination. The discriminating population is 59 of 115. Recorded because a pin count that silently absorbed ten free passes would be the check that cannot fail, in the very field that exists to measure how much the check is worth.
